Guidewire Software’s Cloud Shift Powers Earnings Call
Tipranks - Tipranks - Wed Sep 16, 7:22PM CDT
Guidewire Software Inc. ((GWRE)) has held its Q4 earnings call. Read on for the main highlights of the call.
Guidewire Software Inc. struck an upbeat tone on its latest earnings call, underscoring record recurring revenue, accelerating cloud adoption and expanding profitability. Management acknowledged some expected headwinds from legacy license and services dynamics, but emphasized that subscription, AI and core cloud momentum are firmly reshaping the company’s growth profile.
Annual recurring revenue closed fiscal 2026 at $1.242 billion, rising 19% year over year and topping the high end of guidance. Fully ramped ARR grew an even faster 22%, marking the fourth straight year that fully ramped ARR growth has outpaced overall ARR, signaling durable expansion from existing deals.
Strong Subscription and Total Revenue Growth
Subscription revenue surged to $916 million, up 37% from a year earlier, while subscription and support revenue climbed 33% to $971 million. Total revenue reached $1.475 billion, an increase of 23% that came in ahead of expectations, highlighting the strength of Guidewire’s transition to a subscription-led model.
Cloud ARR jumped 35% year over year and now represents 84% of total ARR, underscoring the rapid migration toward Guidewire Cloud Platform. The company ended the year with 105 customers generating fully ramped ARR above $5 million, up from 86, showing deeper penetration among larger insurers.
Nationwide Cloud Migration and PricingCenter Win
A multiyear deal with Nationwide stood out as a key cloud milestone, as the carrier agreed to move its entire InsuranceSuite estate onto Guidewire’s cloud platform. Nationwide also selected PricingCenter for personal lines pricing and rating, becoming Guidewire’s first U.S. Tier 1 customer for home and auto within that product.
Core Cloud Deal Momentum Across the Portfolio
Guidewire closed 26 core deals in the fourth quarter and 62 for the full year, spanning PolicyCenter, ClaimCenter, BillingCenter and InsuranceNow. Wins included AF Group, MAPFRE U.S., a large Canadian insurer, Definity and several long-standing customers, pointing to broad-based cloud demand across the installed base.
ProNavigator’s Rapid Commercial Traction
ProNavigator’s sales velocity significantly beat internal plans, with 14 wins in the fourth quarter and 28 over the year, driven mainly by cross-sell into existing Guidewire customers. Management highlighted that its AI-driven assistance is being embedded directly into ClaimCenter and PolicyCenter workflows, deepening its strategic value.
PricingCenter Deal Growth and Global Adoption
PricingCenter closed eight deals in the fourth quarter and 12 across fiscal 2026, expanding its footprint among carriers seeking more sophisticated rating. New customers included Nationwide, a Finnish InsuranceSuite customer, Capital Insurance Group, Shelter Insurance and Achmea Farm Insurance in Australia, showing global traction.
Advances in AI Platform and Agentic Capabilities
Developer assistants are now available to all customers and partners, providing AI help within Guidewire’s development environment. The Qusar release introduced an agentic platform that lets insurers build stand-alone AI agents tuned to their own implementations and workflows, running inside core Guidewire systems.
Investments in Implementation Efficiency
Guidewire said new implementation tools and AI-powered project harnesses are materially reducing project complexity and duration. The company plans to roll these capabilities out across all projects and systems integrator partners over the next six months, targeting faster go-lives and lower delivery risk.
Improved Profitability and Gross Margin Performance
Gross profit reached $990 million, up 25% year over year, with overall gross margin at 67%. Subscription and support gross margin rose four points to 74.5%, putting the company close to the high end of its fiscal 2028 margin target and reinforcing the leverage in the cloud model.
Operating Income, Cash Flow and Balance Sheet Strength
Non-GAAP operating income climbed to $340 million, up 63% and above the high end of the outlook, while operating cash flow increased 30% to $390 million. Guidewire ended the quarter with $1.2 billion in cash, cash equivalents and investments, providing ample flexibility for investment and capital returns.
Share Repurchases Reflect Confidence in the Business
The company repurchased $606 million of stock in fiscal 2026, buying back 4.1 million shares at an average price of $148.41. Management said the nearly completed program was made possible by expanding profitability and cash generation and reflects confidence in Guidewire’s long-term trajectory.
Annual gross ARR attrition was less than 1.5% across all ARR and under 1% for core systems, which account for most of the base. Executives described these retention levels at more than $1 billion in ARR as world-class, emphasizing the stickiness of Guidewire’s solutions among insurers.
UnderwritingCenter Progress with Early Customers
Guidewire is working closely with early adopters of UnderwritingCenter and reported encouraging hands-on feedback and traction. Management expects to share more details at its Connections user conference, suggesting the product could become another pillar in the company’s underwriting and decisioning suite.
Broadening Market Reach and Product Investments
Managing general agents and smaller carriers contributed meaningfully to the year’s performance, widening Guidewire’s addressable market beyond large insurers. The company continues to invest in workers’ compensation content, geography-specific tools and its broader product portfolio to deepen relevance across segments.
License revenue fell 7% to $235 million in fiscal 2026 as customers migrated to cloud subscriptions, and management expects license revenue to drop to about $189 million in fiscal 2027. Support revenue is also forecast to decline by about $8 million because cloud customers’ support is bundled within subscription fees.
Services Margin Pressure and Slower Growth
Services gross margin slipped to 12.5% from 12.9%, with management citing investments in capacity and AI capabilities as near-term drags. Services revenue grew 23% to $270 million, but fiscal 2027 revenue is expected to reach around $285 million, indicating more modest growth and margin near 12%.
Attrition and Backlog Dynamics in Fiscal 2027
The fiscal 2027 ARR outlook assumes attrition returns to more normal levels, after record-low churn added roughly one point to fiscal 2026 ARR growth. The ratio of ARR expected to flow from backlog into 2027 is slightly lower, reflecting more ramp events shifting into years two through five rather than the first year.
First-Quarter Margin and Cash Flow Timing Effects
For the first quarter, services revenue is expected around $65 million with services margin roughly breakeven due to the timing of large fixed-fee engagements, leaving total gross margin near 65%. Operating cash flow will be pressured by annual bonuses and commissions tied to fourth-quarter sales, following patterns seen last year.
Leadership Transition in Finance Function
Chief Accounting Officer David Peterson plans to retire in early November, and the CFO praised the strong team he built. Management said the depth of the finance organization leaves Guidewire well positioned to maintain reporting quality and control as the company continues to scale.
Fiscal 2027 Outlook and Forward Guidance
Guidewire projects fiscal 2027 ARR between $1.45 billion and $1.46 billion, implying 18% constant currency growth at the midpoint, with more than half of net new ARR already under contract. Total revenue is expected between $1.707 billion and $1.727 billion, subscription revenue to grow about 31%, subscription and support margins of 75% to 76%, total gross margin of 67% to 68%, non-GAAP operating income of $403 million to $423 million, and operating cash flow of $445 million to $465 million.
Guidewire’s earnings call painted the picture of a cloud-first insurer technology leader turning strong demand into high-margin, recurring revenue growth. While license, support and services margins face manageable headwinds, investors heard a clear message of confidence in the company’s subscription engine, AI capabilities and expanding customer base, setting an upbeat tone for fiscal 2027.

What Happened?
A number of stocks jumped in the afternoon session after softer labor market data tempered expectations for an October interest rate increase by the Federal Reserve.
The latest employment figures signaled a gradual cooling in workforce demand, prompting investors to scale back forecasts of tighter monetary policy from the central bank. When labor market pressures ease, policymakers face less wage-driven inflation risk, reducing the likelihood of additional borrowing cost increases.
For growth-oriented technology businesses, lower projected interest rates are particularly beneficial because their market valuations rely heavily on projected future cash flows. When discount rates stabilize or decline, the present value of those future earnings increases, supporting valuations across the sector as market participants await the release of the Federal Reserve's policy minutes.
The stock market overreacts to news, and big price drops can present good opportunities to buy high-quality stocks.

The previous big move we wrote about was 4 days ago when the stock gained 9.3% on the news that strength across artificial intelligence and technology equities helped lift major market averages, offsetting macroeconomic headwinds from Treasury yields near 24-year highs. Equities showed resilience as strong investor appetite for artificial intelligence hardware and software providers pushed the sector higher for a second straight session. The momentum in tech shares helped counterbalance significant pressure stemming from benchmark Treasury yields trading around multi-decade highs alongside rising crude oil prices.
Typically, higher yields elevate financing costs and weigh on the valuations of growth-oriented companies. However, market participants remained focused on underlying enterprise AI adoption, evaluating incoming corporate earnings reports, and awaiting key macroeconomic data, including the upcoming jobs report.
Guidewire Software is down 13.7% since the beginning of the year, and at $161.98 per share, it is trading 36.3% below its 52-week high of $254.23 from October 2025. Guidewire Names Dan Brown as Chief Product Officer
Mon, October 5, 2026 at 5:55 AM PDT 2 min read
Enterprise software veteran brings 25+ years of product strategy leadership experience to drive Guidewire's product vision, strategy, and roadmap
SAN MATEO, Calif., Oct. 5, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Guidewire (NYSE: GWRE) today announced the appointment of Dan Brown as Chief Product Officer. Reporting to Chief Executive Officer Mike Rosenbaum, Brown will lead Guidewire product strategy and execution, leveraging his deep experience in successfully building and scaling enterprise software organizations, to embed AI across Guidewire's suite of core applications and transform how global P&C insurers underwrite risk and manage claims.
Dan Brown joins Guidewire as Chief Product Officer.
"Dan has a proven record of turning product vision into decisive market execution and rapid enterprise adoption," said Mike Rosenbaum, CEO, Guidewire. "Under his leadership, Guidewire will continue pushing the boundaries and expectations of insurance core applications, helping our customers modernize their operations and take advantage of this historic technology-driven opportunity."
Brown brings more than 25 years of enterprise software experience, leading product strategy for top software companies. He joins Guidewire from Celonis where he served as Chief Product Officer. Prior to that, Brown held the Chief Product Officer role at Certinia and several product, R&D, and leadership positions during his 15-year tenure at Microsoft.
"As I step into this role, what stands out is how closely our customers and partners shape what we build," said Dan Brown, Chief Product Officer, Guidewire. "We're already bringing AI into the products insurers trust, making them more powerful, intuitive, and valuable. I'm excited to work closely with our community to build on that momentum and continue delivering meaningful innovation."
Guidewire is the platform P&C insurers trust to engage, innovate, and grow efficiently. More than 570 insurers in 44 countries, from new ventures to the largest and most complex in the world, rely on Guidewire products. With core systems leveraging data and analytics, digital, and artificial intelligence, Guidewire defines cloud platform excellence for P&C insurers.
We are proud of our unparalleled implementation record, with 1,700+ successful projects supported by the industry's largest R&D team and consulting partner ecosystem. Our marketplace represents the largest partner community in P&C, where customers can access hundreds of applications to accelerate integration, localization, and innovation.
For more information, please visit www.guidewire.com and follow us on X and LinkedIn.

What Happened?
A number of stocks jumped in the afternoon session after strength across artificial intelligence and technology equities helped lift major market averages, offsetting macroeconomic headwinds from Treasury yields near 24-year highs.
Equities showed resilience as strong investor appetite for artificial intelligence hardware and software providers pushed the sector higher for a second straight session. The momentum in tech shares helped counterbalance significant pressure stemming from benchmark Treasury yields trading around multi-decade highs alongside rising crude oil prices. Typically, higher yields elevate financing costs and weigh on the valuations of growth-oriented companies. However, market participants remained focused on underlying enterprise AI adoption, evaluating incoming corporate earnings reports, and awaiting key macroeconomic data, including the upcoming jobs report.
The stock market overreacts to news, and big price drops can present good opportunities to buy high-quality stocks.

According to Reuters, while chipmakers and hardware providers faced steep sell-offs after leaders from Anthropic and OpenAI urged a pause in frontier AI advancement, software stocks bucked the broader tech trend and climbed higher in early trading. Market participants viewed the potential deceleration in AI infrastructure spending as a catalyst to rotate back into traditional enterprise software names like ServiceNow, Salesforce, and Adobe.Investors have increasingly feared that unchecked AI progress could yield autonomous agents capable of bypassing traditional software interfaces entirely. A development freeze limits that threat. It also gives incumbent platforms breathing room to package AI as a feature within their own ecosystems, preserving their recurring revenue without the immediate risk of frontier models rendering their core software obsolete.
Broadly, these SaaS companies are perceived as less vulnerable to a sudden halt in hyperscaler capital expenditures; instead, they offer steady recurring revenue streams and are positioned to benefit from a more deliberate, measured integration of existing AI tools into corporate workflows rather than a frantic, capital-intensive race for raw compute power.

Management linked its ability to execute the repurchases to expanding profitability, cash generation and confidence in the long-term durability of the business.

Gross profit increased 25% to $990 million, while overall gross margin was 67%. Subscription and support gross margin improved 4 percentage points to 74.5%. For fiscal 2027, Guidewire expects operating cash flow of $445 million to $465 million. The company also projects non-GAAP operating income of $403 million to $423 million and total gross margin of 67% to 68%. Capital expenditures are expected to range from $23 million to $28 million, including approximately $17 million of capitalized software development costs. Guidewire Software's Cloud Migration, AI Strategy Support Durable Growth, RBC Capital Markets Says
Guidewire Software's (GWRE) contracted cloud migration and growing adoption of artificial intelligence products support a durable growth outlook, RBC Capital Markets said in a note Tuesday after meeting with company executives.
Guidewire still has about 100 customers expected to migrate from on-premises systems to the cloud over the next four to five years, the investment firm said. Customers often expand their use of the company's products during the transition, providing visibility into the 18% annual recurring revenue growth forecast for fiscal 2027, according to the note.
ProNavigator has generated 28 deals with an approximately 30% increase in annual contract value, while the Underwriting Center platform has early customer deployments and could open a multi-billion-dollar total addressable market opportunity, the firm said.
Guidewire's gross annual recurring revenue attrition was below 1% in fiscal 2026, while the number of customers generating at least $5 million in fully ramped annual recurring revenue rose to 105 from 86 a year earlier, the note said.
RBC Capital Markets maintained an outperform rating on Guidewire, with a price target of $215.

Guidewire Software’s Cloud Shift Powers Earnings Call
Tipranks - Tipranks - Wed Sep 16, 7:22PM CDT
Guidewire Software Inc. ((GWRE)) has held its Q4 earnings call. Read on for the main highlights of the call.
Guidewire Software Inc. struck an upbeat tone on its latest earnings call, underscoring record recurring revenue, accelerating cloud adoption and expanding profitability. Management acknowledged some expected headwinds from legacy license and services dynamics, but emphasized that subscription, AI and core cloud momentum are firmly reshaping the company’s growth profile.
Annual recurring revenue closed fiscal 2026 at $1.242 billion, rising 19% year over year and topping the high end of guidance. Fully ramped ARR grew an even faster 22%, marking the fourth straight year that fully ramped ARR growth has outpaced overall ARR, signaling durable expansion from existing deals.
Strong Subscription and Total Revenue Growth
Subscription revenue surged to $916 million, up 37% from a year earlier, while subscription and support revenue climbed 33% to $971 million. Total revenue reached $1.475 billion, an increase of 23% that came in ahead of expectations, highlighting the strength of Guidewire’s transition to a subscription-led model.
Cloud ARR jumped 35% year over year and now represents 84% of total ARR, underscoring the rapid migration toward Guidewire Cloud Platform. The company ended the year with 105 customers generating fully ramped ARR above $5 million, up from 86, showing deeper penetration among larger insurers.
Nationwide Cloud Migration and PricingCenter Win
A multiyear deal with Nationwide stood out as a key cloud milestone, as the carrier agreed to move its entire InsuranceSuite estate onto Guidewire’s cloud platform. Nationwide also selected PricingCenter for personal lines pricing and rating, becoming Guidewire’s first U.S. Tier 1 customer for home and auto within that product.
Core Cloud Deal Momentum Across the Portfolio
Guidewire closed 26 core deals in the fourth quarter and 62 for the full year, spanning PolicyCenter, ClaimCenter, BillingCenter and InsuranceNow. Wins included AF Group, MAPFRE U.S., a large Canadian insurer, Definity and several long-standing customers, pointing to broad-based cloud demand across the installed base.
ProNavigator’s Rapid Commercial Traction
ProNavigator’s sales velocity significantly beat internal plans, with 14 wins in the fourth quarter and 28 over the year, driven mainly by cross-sell into existing Guidewire customers. Management highlighted that its AI-driven assistance is being embedded directly into ClaimCenter and PolicyCenter workflows, deepening its strategic value.
PricingCenter Deal Growth and Global Adoption
PricingCenter closed eight deals in the fourth quarter and 12 across fiscal 2026, expanding its footprint among carriers seeking more sophisticated rating. New customers included Nationwide, a Finnish InsuranceSuite customer, Capital Insurance Group, Shelter Insurance and Achmea Farm Insurance in Australia, showing global traction.
Advances in AI Platform and Agentic Capabilities
Developer assistants are now available to all customers and partners, providing AI help within Guidewire’s development environment. The Qusar release introduced an agentic platform that lets insurers build stand-alone AI agents tuned to their own implementations and workflows, running inside core Guidewire systems.
Investments in Implementation Efficiency
Guidewire said new implementation tools and AI-powered project harnesses are materially reducing project complexity and duration. The company plans to roll these capabilities out across all projects and systems integrator partners over the next six months, targeting faster go-lives and lower delivery risk.
Improved Profitability and Gross Margin Performance
Gross profit reached $990 million, up 25% year over year, with overall gross margin at 67%. Subscription and support gross margin rose four points to 74.5%, putting the company close to the high end of its fiscal 2028 margin target and reinforcing the leverage in the cloud model.
Operating Income, Cash Flow and Balance Sheet Strength
Non-GAAP operating income climbed to $340 million, up 63% and above the high end of the outlook, while operating cash flow increased 30% to $390 million. Guidewire ended the quarter with $1.2 billion in cash, cash equivalents and investments, providing ample flexibility for investment and capital returns.
Share Repurchases Reflect Confidence in the Business
The company repurchased $606 million of stock in fiscal 2026, buying back 4.1 million shares at an average price of $148.41. Management said the nearly completed program was made possible by expanding profitability and cash generation and reflects confidence in Guidewire’s long-term trajectory.
Annual gross ARR attrition was less than 1.5% across all ARR and under 1% for core systems, which account for most of the base. Executives described these retention levels at more than $1 billion in ARR as world-class, emphasizing the stickiness of Guidewire’s solutions among insurers.
UnderwritingCenter Progress with Early Customers
Guidewire is working closely with early adopters of UnderwritingCenter and reported encouraging hands-on feedback and traction. Management expects to share more details at its Connections user conference, suggesting the product could become another pillar in the company’s underwriting and decisioning suite.
Broadening Market Reach and Product Investments
Managing general agents and smaller carriers contributed meaningfully to the year’s performance, widening Guidewire’s addressable market beyond large insurers. The company continues to invest in workers’ compensation content, geography-specific tools and its broader product portfolio to deepen relevance across segments.
License revenue fell 7% to $235 million in fiscal 2026 as customers migrated to cloud subscriptions, and management expects license revenue to drop to about $189 million in fiscal 2027. Support revenue is also forecast to decline by about $8 million because cloud customers’ support is bundled within subscription fees.
Services Margin Pressure and Slower Growth
Services gross margin slipped to 12.5% from 12.9%, with management citing investments in capacity and AI capabilities as near-term drags. Services revenue grew 23% to $270 million, but fiscal 2027 revenue is expected to reach around $285 million, indicating more modest growth and margin near 12%.
Attrition and Backlog Dynamics in Fiscal 2027
The fiscal 2027 ARR outlook assumes attrition returns to more normal levels, after record-low churn added roughly one point to fiscal 2026 ARR growth. The ratio of ARR expected to flow from backlog into 2027 is slightly lower, reflecting more ramp events shifting into years two through five rather than the first year.
First-Quarter Margin and Cash Flow Timing Effects
For the first quarter, services revenue is expected around $65 million with services margin roughly breakeven due to the timing of large fixed-fee engagements, leaving total gross margin near 65%. Operating cash flow will be pressured by annual bonuses and commissions tied to fourth-quarter sales, following patterns seen last year.
Leadership Transition in Finance Function
Chief Accounting Officer David Peterson plans to retire in early November, and the CFO praised the strong team he built. Management said the depth of the finance organization leaves Guidewire well positioned to maintain reporting quality and control as the company continues to scale.
Fiscal 2027 Outlook and Forward Guidance
Guidewire projects fiscal 2027 ARR between $1.45 billion and $1.46 billion, implying 18% constant currency growth at the midpoint, with more than half of net new ARR already under contract. Total revenue is expected between $1.707 billion and $1.727 billion, subscription revenue to grow about 31%, subscription and support margins of 75% to 76%, total gross margin of 67% to 68%, non-GAAP operating income of $403 million to $423 million, and operating cash flow of $445 million to $465 million.
Guidewire’s earnings call painted the picture of a cloud-first insurer technology leader turning strong demand into high-margin, recurring revenue growth. While license, support and services margins face manageable headwinds, investors heard a clear message of confidence in the company’s subscription engine, AI capabilities and expanding customer base, setting an upbeat tone for fiscal 2027.
